tasks.q: A council closes its phone line and moves all forms online. What is the cultural issue?
a: People without internet access or confidence can no longer reach the service
tasks.fb: Efficiency for most can mean exclusion for some.

tasks.q: Is each change mainly a benefit or a drawback of daily life moving online?
items: Paying a bill at midnight from home
A high street with empty shops
Older relatives cut off from services
Seeing a doctor by video from a rural village
Expecting everyone to own a smartphone
tasks.fb: Almost every change here has both columns filled in.

tasks.q: A school sets all homework online, to be submitted through a website. How is each group affected?

stakeholders.name: Pupils with a laptop and fast broadband
Pupils sharing one phone at home
Pupils with no internet at home

tasks.fb: The divide is rarely about who owns a computer: it is about connection, time on a device, and somewhere quiet to use it.
tasks.title: Online-only homework: who is affected?

tasks.q: Which is a cause of the digital divide rather than an effect?
a: The cost of broadband in rural areas
tasks.fb: Causes create the gap; effects follow from it.

tasks.q: Which of these would genuinely narrow the digital divide? Select all that apply.
opts: Lending laptops to pupils who need them
Free wifi in libraries and community centres
Training sessions for people new to the internet
Keeping a phone option for council services
correct: Lending laptops to pupils who need them
Free wifi in libraries and community centres
Training sessions for people new to the internet
Keeping a phone option for council services
tasks.fb: Access, cost, skills and an alternative route in.

tasks.q: Why is handing out devices not enough on its own?
a: Without a connection, support and skills, the device goes unused
tasks.fb: All three barriers have to come down together.

tasks.q: Is each point a benefit or a drawback of globalisation?
items: Products cost less to make, so prices fall
Jobs move to countries with lower wages
Skilled work can be done from anywhere
Working conditions may be poorer where costs are lowest
tasks.fb: Whether it looks good depends on where you are standing, which is the point of the question.

tasks.q: Why is globalisation a cultural issue rather than only an economic one?
a: It changes how communities work, what they watch and which languages dominate
tasks.fb: Shared platforms make cultures more alike, which some see as loss.

tasks.q: A warehouse replaces pickers with robots. What is the strongest exam point?
a: The company saves money and works faster, but staff lose jobs and may not have the skills for the new ones
tasks.fb: Benefit, cost, and who carries each.

tasks.q: Which is a cultural impact of remote working?
a: Town centres built around office workers lose their customers
tasks.fb: Cultural impacts are about how people live, not the technology itself.

tasks.q: A bank closes its last branch in a small town and moves everything to its app. How is each group affected?

stakeholders.name: Customers who bank on their phone
Local small businesses paying in cash
Nearby shops relying on passing trade

tasks.fb: This is the digital divide in one street: convenience for some, exclusion for others.

a: Most customers gain a service available at any hour, but those without a smartphone lose access entirely, so the bank should keep a staffed option
Closing branches is bad for old people
tasks.fb: Both sides, named groups, and a defensible position.

stations.name: Final challenge: who is left behind?

tasks.q: Which cultural issue does each statement describe?
items: A village with no fast broadband
A support centre opened in another country
Staff working three days a week from home
A pupil doing homework on a phone screen
The same games played in a hundred countries
A supermarket replacing tills with machines
Older people unable to book a doctor online
A small firm selling worldwide from a bedroom
tasks.fb: These three words cover most of the cultural marks on the paper.

info.title: Not just rural
info.text: The divide is often sharpest within cities, where cost rather than coverage is the barrier.

info.title: Homework gap
info.text: During school closures, the difference between pupils with a laptop and those without became one of the clearest examples of the divide.

info.title: Follow the sun
info.text: Global firms pass work between offices in different time zones so a project is worked on continuously.

info.title: Not new
info.text: Every wave of technology has moved work: looms, production lines, spreadsheets. What changes is how fast and which jobs.

info.title: Language online
info.text: A small number of languages dominate the web, which pushes speakers of smaller languages towards them.

info.title: The 15-minute answer
info.text: Examiners say cultural questions are often answered with opinion and no reasons. Reasons are where the marks are.
